reason: The mirror of the publication's counters onto the pass's copy allocates once, the array the rows' node lists are cut from, in place of two allocations per Instance, which takes the publication through the reconciler below its recorded bytes: the pods-listed rows 20,268 allocations and 2,263,880 bytes at 1,000 Instances (from 22,272 and 2,492,440), 75,244 and 8,398,824 at 4,000 (from 83,260 and 9,313,064); the rows with a list of their own 120,329 and 15,711,504 (from 122,331 and 15,940,064), 475,315 and 64,589,688 (from 483,331 and 65,503,928). The publication's three groupings of the pods by Instance are each built from one array after one count per Instance, where each grew a map and one slice per Instance from nothing: the pods-listed rows 31,473 → 28,446 allocations and 3.67 → 3.32 MB at 1,000 Instances, 119,508 → 107,453 and 14.7 → 13.3 MB at 4,000; the rows with a list of their own 131,532 → 128,504 and 17.1 → 16.8 MB, 519,579 → 507,524 and 70.9 → 69.5 MB. The publication at the end of one pass over a replica at rest: the promotion and the status write read one cached list of the Component's pods, one EndpointSlice list, one read per Node under the pods, no live read of the replica (the status write decides on the pass's copy and reads the replica live only when the copy calls for a write), no write. The bytes of one publication are held beside its allocations. When the pass took the pods before (the engine's list) and wrote none since, the publication reads that list and lists nothing itself (the pods-listed rows): 35,486 and 135,533 allocations, 4.2 and 16.6 MB, at 1,000 and 4,000 Instances against 135,547 and 535,604 allocations, 17.6 and 72.8 MB, with a list of its own. While the status write's compare walked the rows by reflection the same rows read 61,532 and 239,677 allocations, 5.1 and 20.6 MB, and 161,595 and 639,750, 18.6 and 76.8 MB; with the write's one live read of the replica per publication besides, 67,693 and 263,847, 5.9 and 24.4 MB, and 167,753 and 663,914, 19.4 and 80.6 MB. The fake client encodes and decodes every object it serves as JSON, so most of the count with a list is the stand-in's: the list of 4,000 pods alone is about 400,000 allocations. The deadline step the write runs last (reconcileHeldDeadlines) converts only the rows with an operation open and reads nothing at rest, where no row has one: readySince/1000/allocations 135,543 → 131,532, readySince/1000/bytes 17,612,760 → 17,119,712, readySince/1000/pods-listed/allocations 35,486 → 31,473, readySince/1000/pods-listed/bytes 4,165,128 → 3,672,216, readySince/4000/allocations 535,604 → 519,579, readySince/4000/bytes 72,833,256 → 70,896,392, readySince/4000/pods-listed/allocations 135,533 → 119,508, readySince/4000/pods-listed/bytes 16,642,408 → 14,705,544. The promotion decides on the pass's copy and reads the replica live only when the copy calls for a write, and its per-Instance pod revisions are cut from one array: readySince/1000/pods-listed/allocations 28,446 → 22,286, readySince/1000/pods-listed/bytes 3,320,008 → 2,546,784, readySince/4000/pods-listed/allocations 107,453 → 83,288, readySince/4000/pods-listed/bytes 13,290,776 → 9,531,232; the rows with a list of their own move by the same promotion (128,504 → 122,349 and 507,524 → 483,360), inside their band and re-recorded all the same. Re-recorded with the pass's list handing its buckets by Instance to every reader that asks for the same list, so the promotion and the status write of a publication over the pass's list bucket the pods once between them, and not at all when the engine read the list first: the publication over the pass's list 20,268 / 75,244 to 20,250 / 75,202 allocations and 2.26 MB / 8.40 MB to 2.06 MB / 7.58 MB; the publication that lists 120,329 / 475,315 to 120,321 / 475,296 allocations and 15.71 MB / 64.59 MB to 15.61 MB / 64.18 MB. Re-recorded with the publication building no list per Instance (status.AppendUniqueNodes cuts every row's node list from one array, the pods that report are read in place when none is left out, and the live pods are counted without a list): readySince/1000/pods-listed/allocations 20,250 → 18,252, readySince/1000/pods-listed/bytes 2,058,824 → 2,051,216, readySince/4000/pods-listed/allocations 75,202 → 67,204, readySince/4000/pods-listed/bytes 7,578,888 → 7,548,432; the rows with a list of their own move by the same two allocations per Instance (120,321 → 118,322 and 475,296 → 467,298), the smallest of three re-recordings.
